messages:
sam (AE): Heads-up: Enterprise prospect wants a single-file PDF for vendor risk that proves we can deliver immutable audit exports and SIEM ingestion examples. They also asked for retention tiers (90d vs 365d) pricing. Can ops/security confirm exact wording we can share?

raje (SE): We should include concrete examples: S3 export path naming (s3://redwood-audit-exports/<customer-id>/YYYY/MM/DD/), an example HEC config for Splunk, and a sample signed manifest (sha256).

katie (InfoSec): Short answer for questionnaire: \"Audit and administrative events are recorded and retained per customer-configurable policies. Exports can be sent to customer-managed S3 or forwarded to customer SIEM via syslog/HTTP collectors. For Hosted we provide a default searchable retention of 90 days; Dedicated/Private allow custom retention and WORM options.\" I'll add one-liners for chain-of-custody and tamper evidence.

oliver (SRE): Operational facts: export files are NDJSON, gzipped, and contain a file-level sha256 checksum and a signed manifest (we sign with our pipeline key and include timestamp). We can produce a time-stamped, signed bundle for PoC on request. For true WORM we rely on customer-provided WORM S3; we can write to that target.

procurement-bot (automated): Note: Pricing flag - short PoC exports are covered under onboarding credits. Longer-term export/egress fees apply. See pricing matrix: https://intra.redwood/pricing/export-egress

sam (AE): Can we show an example manifest + sample ndjson line (redacted) so their VRM team can verify fields? Keep it minimal but shows admin key rollover, a model deploy, and a failed token usage.

raje (SE): I'll paste a tiny sample ndjson (redacted) and a manifest template to include in the PDF.

```
{"timestamp":"2026-03-18T22:15:04Z","actor":"admin@acme.com","actor_role":"admin","actor_ip":"18.205.23.4","action":"key.rotate","object":"api_key:xxxx","request_id":"req_9b8f","outcome":"success"}
{"timestamp":"2026-03-19T03:02:11Z","actor":"svc-model-deploy","actor_role":"service","actor_ip":"10.45.2.7","action":"model.deploy","object":"model:gptx-7b-v2","request_id":"req_9c1a","outcome":"success"}
{"timestamp":"2026-03-19T05:10:52Z","actor":"unknown","actor_role":"unknown","actor_ip":"203.0.113.77","action":"auth.token","object":"token:hashed","request_id":"req_9d2b","outcome":"failure"}
```

```
manifest.json
{
  "export_start":"2026-03-18T00:00:00Z",
  "export_end":"2026-03-20T00:00:00Z",
  "files":[
    {"path":"s3://redwood-audit-exports/acme/2026/03/18/logs-20260318-1.ndjson.gz","sha256":"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924...","size":12345}
  ],
  "manifest_signed_by":"pipeline-signing-key-v1",
  "manifest_signature":"MEUCIQD..."
}
```

katie (InfoSec): Wording for immutability: \"We provide append-only audit records and pipeline-signed manifests for tamper-evidence. For customers requiring technical WORM guarantees we support direct export to customer-managed WORM-capable storage and can integrate with HSM-backed KMS to restrict key rotation.\" Good?

oliver (SRE): Also include a short snippet showing Splunk HEC ingest via curl and an example syslog-forwarder config.

```
curl -k -H "Authorization: Splunk <HEC-TOKEN>" \
  https://splunk.example.com:8088/services/collector/event \
  -d '{"event":"<ndjson-line>","sourcetype":"redwood:audit"}'
```

# syslog-forwarder.conf (excerpt)
input(type="imudp" port="514")
action(type="omfwd" target="splunk-collector.example.com" port="514" protocol="tcp")
```

sam (AE): Procurement asked about per-GB egress numbers for 365d vs 90d. Can finance give a quick estimate we can include?

procurement-bot (automated): Estimated egress for customer-managed S3 export: $0.09/GB per month (varies by region). Long-term storage on S3 Glacier/Archive would be lower for retained copies. Final numbers go in SOW.

raje (SE): For the PDF let's include: 1) redacted ndjson excerpt, 2) manifest template with signature note, 3) Splunk + syslog example, 4) retention options table (text), 5) statement on immutability and WORM options.

katie (InfoSec): I'll drop a one-paragraph SIG/CAIQ-friendly answer for Q: \"Can you export admin logs to customer SIEM?\" Suggested: \"Yes. Administrative and API events can be exported to customer-managed S3 or forwarded to SIEMs via syslog or HTTP collectors. Exports include signed manifests and checksums for integrity verification. Retention and immutability options are deployment-dependent.\"

oliver (SRE): Operational note: to generate a signed bundle we need a ticket with start/end times and justification. Allow 2biz days for the signed artifact. Regular exports can be automated via Console.

sam (AE): Perfect. Who will assemble the PDF and drive to the customer?

raje (SE): I can assemble the tech appendix. sam, you take the final send.

katie (InfoSec): I'll add the SIG snippet and the immutability blurb.

sam (AE): Thanks — target to deliver PDF + temp S3 link by EOD tomorrow. If any legal/perm issues pop up, tag me. :thumbsup:
